documents.unit: Junta de Gobierno, Universidad de Puerto Rico (system-wide, applies to Mayagüez)
documents.title: Política de Uso de Inteligencia Artificial en la Universidad de Puerto Rico (Certificación 66, 2024-2025)
documents.summary: System-wide UPR regulation (Spanish) setting principles for AI use in administration, teaching and research, with sections on responsibilities, IP, data security, procurement and discipline. For students it says AI use depends on professor authorization, bans substituting intellectual effort in assessments unless the professor explicitly allows it, and requires AI rules in every syllabus. Most of the text concerns institutional governance, vendor review and data protection.
documents.stance_why: For student coursework the document sets no rule of its own: students "podrá utilizar IA ... siempre que sea autorizado por sus profesores", and assessment use is barred "a menos que el profesor haya impartido instrucciones explícitas", and each syllabus must state the rules. The decision is handed to instructors, so delegates, not restrict, even though unauthorized assessment use is misconduct.

units.why: The purpose clause says the policy exists "para establecer los principios para el uso responsable y ético" of AI in administrative, academic and research areas, which is an institution-wide framework statement (P56).

units.policy: The Policy's purpose is to establish the principles for responsible and ethical use of AI technology in administrative, academic and research areas.

The student-side prohibition is the separate unit on the same sentence.

A split the sanctions pointer into its own unit (P81); it is the same sentence and adds no procedure, so it is folded into this unit.

notes: Spanish-language system-wide UPR policy shared with Rio Piedras; no campus, college or department policy found. Policies are normalized in English; anchors are quoted from the Spanish text. Most units concern administration, data security and governance rather than student coursework. Reconciled from coders A and B: B's unit segmentation used as the base (it splits compound sentences more finely); A's unit coverage was fully matched.
